paragraphs.source_en: The army was ‘permitted and compelled to immediately punish in the most severe manner, or attack and annihilate in the event of [armed] resistance, those who in any manner opposed the carrying out of government decrees, or acts for the defense of the homeland and the establishment of public order’.** From May until the end of summer, Talat Pasha issued further written orders, usually sent as telegrams from his personal telegraph machine in his home.* These telegrams sent to provincial governors in central and eastern Anatolia ordered them to use the army to deport Armenian men, women, and children to Ras al- Ayn and Deir ez-Zor in the Syrian desert and other camps along the Euphrates, under the oversight of the Interior Ministry.

paragraphs.source_en: At the same time, acting on secret, oral orders from CUP central committee members including Dr. Nazim, Dr. Bahaettin Sakir— the son of refugees from Bulgaria and head of the Special Organisation, formed from self-sacrificing CUP volunteers—outfitted, paid, and commanded armed gangs made up of Southeastern European and Caucasian migrants, Turks, and Kurds to annihilate the caravans as they moved out of the towns.*° According to the memoir of a former CUP central committee member, the gendarmerie received orders to turn deported Armenians over to bands of Special Organisation irregulars who were waiting for them at prearranged locations ‘like vultures’. These caravans ‘were dispatched like herds of sheep to the slaughterhouse’.” The Armenian woman Pailadzo Captanian of the Black Sea port of Samsun survived the deportation.

paragraphs.source_en: Her three- and fiveyear-old sons also lived because she gave them to a Greek family for safekeeping at the beginning of the forced journey. Her husband, however, did not survive, because at the beginning of the 438 THE OTTOMANS forced marches, men were separated from women and children, tied together with ropes in small groups, taken to the outskirts of their towns, and shot dead, axed, or bayoneted. Pailadzo Captanian kept a diary recording the gruesome events that unfolded.** At the beginning of July 1915, the Armenians of Samsun began their thousand-kilometre forced march by way of Aleppo to Deir ez-Zor in the Syrian desert, a wasteland not suitable for sustaining the lives of thousands of survivors weakened by a harrowing journey.
